script: This is seventeen seconds of phone video. Just me, walking down a hallway. That's all SamWorld needs to build a world.

SamWorld pulls twenty-five frames and sends them to a GPU worker on Modal. It rebuilds the hallway as a one-million-point cloud, at real scale. Six point eight metres long. Two point three metres high.
Next, SAM 3.1 outlines the objects. Nine of them, doors and doormats, tracked across ten different views. Muse Spark names each one, and lifts it into 3D space.
Then you type a world. A haunted Victorian library corridor, lit by candles. Muse turns that one sentence into a plan for every wall, the floor, the ceiling, and every object it found.

Muse Image, Meta's image model, paints every surface from that plan. Damask walls. Worn oak floors. A smoke-stained ceiling. And SAM 3D turns the objects SAM found into real 3D models, placed right back where they stand.

And this is not a picture. You're standing inside the hallway, rebuilt in 3D from that one clip. Walk forward, and the haunted library spreads across the real walls. Now turn around. Every door is carved mahogany, and every mat, a worn Persian rug.
Phone video in. Explorable world out. In the browser, or on a Meta Quest. SamWorld. Built with Muse, SAM 3.1, SAM 3D, and Modal.
